related_questions.question: Is the COVID pandemic still happening?

text_blocks.snippet: While the World Health Organization (WHO) declared an end to the COVID-19 public health emergency (PHEIC) on May 5, 2023, COVID-19 continues to circulate. Whether it's still considered a pandemic depends on the definition used, and experts are uncertain about its pandemic status. As of July 22, 2025, COVID-19 remains a significant public health concern with ongoing monitoring and vaccination efforts.

list.title: End of PHEIC:
list.snippet: The WHO's declaration of the end of the PHEIC signifies a change in the global health emergency status, but it doesn't mean the virus is gone.

list.title: Ongoing Circulation:
list.snippet: COVID-19 continues to circulate, and while the severity of cases has decreased due to vaccinations and other factors, it still poses a risk.

list.title: Definition Matters:
list.snippet: The term "pandemic" can be interpreted in different ways. Some definitions focus on the geographical spread of a disease, while others emphasize its impact on public health.

list.title: Continued Monitoring:
list.snippet: The WHO and other health organizations continue to monitor the situation, track new variants, and update recommendations for vaccinations.

list.title: Vaccination Efforts:
list.snippet: COVID-19 vaccines remain available and are updated to address new variants. The WHO also continues to evaluate the effectiveness of approved vaccines.
